short: Took America into a European war, then failed to take it into the peace he designed.
full:
Wilson's first term produced the Federal Reserve Act of 1913, the Clayton Antitrust Act, and the federal income tax, and he was re-elected in 1916 on having kept the country out of the war in Europe. Unrestricted German submarine warfare and the Zimmermann Telegram changed that; he asked Congress for a declaration on 2 April 1917.

Two million American troops reached France, tipping a stalemated conflict. His Fourteen Points framed the armistice, and he crossed the Atlantic to negotiate at Versailles in person, securing the League of Nations. The Senate then refused to ratify. Campaigning for the treaty, he collapsed in Colorado in September 1919 and suffered a severe stroke days later; his wife and his physician concealed the extent of it for the remaining seventeen months of his term. His administration also resegregated much of the federal civil service.
